title: Adaptive kernel discovery and prefill choreography benchmarking suite
creator: Jordan Patel
description: Goal: build a reproducible benchmark harness and workload suite that exercises kernel-selection heuristics, new attention optimizations, and prefill/decode scheduling policies together. This ticket covers: (1) a deterministic multiplexing harness to run many model+kernel combinations per run; (2) a traffic-mirroring workload generator that replays production prefix+prompt mixes with controlled noise; (3) anchor baselines and a stability lockfile format for CI to detect regressions from kernel routing and prefill changes. The intent is to enable short, automatable runs that expose regressions in latency P99/P999 and decode throughput across representative cohorts.
acceptance_criteria: A harness binary (or container) that can execute a configurable matrix of model variants, kernel candidates, and prefill/decode schedules in < 90 minutes for the canonical 12k sample suite.
Traffic-mirroring generator with knobs for prefix-length distribution, batch concurrency, and KV-cache hit ratios plus a reproducible seed file format.
Anchor baseline files committed to runtime-1.21 branch and a lockfile format documented in Confluence with instructions for regenerating.

CI integration: two perf gates in CircleCI/GitHub Actions: quick smoke for PRs (10m) and nightly stability run (90m). PR gate fails on >3% P99 latency regression or >5% throughput drop against anchors.
Dashboard panel in Console showing per-kernel latency breakdown, pipeline-stage durations (prefill, kv-lookup, decode), and cohort-level diffs against anchors.
Runbook for triage when CI gate trips linking to suggested mitigation stairs (fallback kernel, prefilling-throttle, ephemeral shard increase).
Telemetry schema changes are backwards-compatible and landed in telemetry proto v3.
plan: Phase A (2w): prototype harness prototype that runs 1 model across 3 kernels with deterministic seeds and collects stage-level timings.
Phase B (1w): build traffic-mirroring generator, collect production prefix histograms, and create canonical 12k sample set.
Phase C (1w): anchor baseline collection and lockfile format; define regression thresholds with SRE.
Phase D (1w): CI gates and dashboard integration; document runbook and onboarding guide.
Phase E (buffer 1w): address flakiness, tune thresholds, and finalize PRs.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy production traces cause non-deterministic CI failures. Mitigation: seed multiplexor + deterministic synthetic noise layer and per-run seed lockfile.
Risk: long-run nightly suite consumes expensive GPU budget. Mitigation: two-level runs (PR smoke small sample, nightly extended) and sample stratification to reduce full-run cost.
Risk: changes in telemetry proto break dashboard queries. Mitigation: proto compatibility checks and shadow dashboard for the first week.
Risk: kernel-specific micro-optimizations mask decode problems. Mitigation: instrument and assert stage-level durations (prefill, kv, decode) not just end-to-end.
Risk: CI gate thresholds too tight/loose. Mitigation: iterate thresholds across 20 warm-up nightly runs before enforcement.
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on co-exercising kernel selection and prefill scheduling; work that changes kernel routing logic belongs in separate feature tickets that will reference this suite as a dependency.
We will reuse existing perf infra where possible (bench-corral jobs and the kernel-prober library) but the harness will be a standalone container to simplify CI integration.
When a PR trips the CI gate, the failure artifact should include the run id, the failing cohort, stage-level diffs, and a minimal repro seedset.
Coordinate with the Dedicated team for any tests that need reserved capacity to avoid noisy multi-tenant interference.
